disclaimer: Demo project using public and simulated data. Not a licensed insurance product, not legal or compliance advice.
reading_note: Numbers under 'dataset' and 'pii_masking' are measured. Numbers under 'simulated_layers' derive from assumptions in config/assumptions.yaml and are not observations of a real insurer's operations.

governance.auto_deny_note: the system can auto-approve but never auto-deny

extraction.accuracy_caveat: NOT a production accuracy estimate. The narratives were generated from templates and the regular expressions were written against those templates, so this figure is close to circular. The hand-written paraphrase set in tests/fixtures was also used while tuning, so no genuinely held-out evaluation exists: all text in this project is synthetic. Read this as 'the regression suite passes', not as evidence the extractor would handle real claimant writing.

fraud_model.label_caveat: fraud_reported is a reported flag, not an adjudicated finding
fraud_model.precision_caveat: the ~25% base rate here is far above a real auto portfolio, so precision is optimistic and would fall sharply in production

triage_routing.stp_caveat: The STP rate is low because of this dataset, not the design: most claims here are large (median ~$58k) and 24.7% carry the reported-fraud flag, so they fail the low-severity or low-fraud test. A realistic auto book would fast-track far more.
